response: Follow-up recommendations for abnormal Papanicolaou smears do not significantly influence patient adherence. Adherence to follow-up was found to be low regardless of the type of follow-up advised. However, the use of up to 3 reminders was shown to improve adherence. This suggests that allocating resources to effective methods for improving adherence to follow-up of abnormal results may be more important than the specific follow-up procedure recommended.
